manifest.hypothesis: On the reference path no generation whose revocation was acknowledged becomes authorizable through any enumerated crash, power-loss or leadership schedule, and recovery is consistent: the history a recovery returns is the acknowledged prefix plus at most the record in flight, never a reordered, duplicated or dropped acknowledged record, and a log and its protected anchor that disagree are classified as the table of crates/ptr-ledger/src/acknowledged.rs says (a log ahead of its anchor is kept, a log behind it is refused). Arms: A, PTRLOG02 FileLedger recovered against the anchor the host holds; B, AcknowledgedLedger with its ProtectedAnchor, crashed at the four failpoints of the log append and the four of the anchor publication (write, fsync, rename, directory fsync); C, RaftEngineLedger crashed at the three failpoints of raft-engine; D, three in-process RaftNode members on a deterministic router (isolation with a minority proposal, term change, restarts, message drop, duplication and reordering). Failure classes, kept distinct: process abort keeps the page cache (an in-process panic at a failpoint, and a child process that calls abort()); power loss keeps the synced prefix of each file and a seeded subset of what was written after it (none, all, a prefix, half, 512-byte holes), a fsync-honest crash-image model and not a real power cut. Seeded workloads of 6 to 14 events over 3 or 4 subjects, every history holding a revoke-then-recommit. An independent oracle (about sixty lines, no code shared with the product) says for every (subject, generation) whether an action may proceed and what the generation's standing is; it is compared with PtrRuntime::replay, authorize_action and generation_validity over every recovered history. Baselines: B0, the same workload without a fault; B1, naive recovery (the log alone, tail trimmed, whatever is left trusted). Controls: an fsync-lie image, outside the honest model, must fool B1 with a stale revocation and be refused by the anchored product. Stated limits: RaftEngineLedger has no anchor, so after a lie it opens on fewer records without error (undetected_rollback, descriptive, no product work); power loss is the fsync-honest crash-image model, and the filesystem is recorded; the durability probe sees file data pages and not directory entries. The directory fsync of the anchor's publication is a failpoint position whose effect is taken on trust (the harness checks that the directory synchronization is entered, not that the kernel wrote the entry), and so is the order of persisting and sending inside a Raft member. Arm D has clean close and reopen only: no power-loss image of the raft-rs storage. A power-loss image whose bytes after the synced length are all zero must recover (a refusal is unjustified_refusals); a refusal of any other image with zeroed sectors is allowed (fail closed) within a pinned share of those recoveries (refusal_share_excess); the evidence is about the failpoint-instrumented build. This experiment supersedes L001.

manifest.falsification: The run is invalid (vacuous) and counts as falsified if any coverage prerequisite is unmet: workloads_file < 6, workloads_ack < 6, workloads_engine < 2, scenarios_raft < 10, scenarios_checked < 10, recoveries_file < 600, recoveries_ack < 1000, recoveries_engine < 250, members_replayed < 70, failpoint_hits.ledger_before_record_write < 20, failpoint_hits.ledger_after_length_before_payload < 20, failpoint_hits.ledger_after_payload_before_sync < 20, failpoint_hits.ledger_after_sync_before_memory < 20, failpoint_hits.anchor_after_scratch_write_before_sync < 20, failpoint_hits.anchor_after_scratch_sync_before_rename < 20, failpoint_hits.anchor_after_rename_before_dir_sync < 20, failpoint_hits.anchor_after_dir_sync < 20, failpoint_hits.engine_append < 20, failpoint_hits.engine_write < 20, failpoint_hits.engine_sync < 20, failpoint_hits.ledger_sync_parent < 20, images_lost_bytes < 1000, rename_image_pairs < 50, lie_images < 100, child_aborts_file < 24, child_aborts_ack < 48, child_aborts_engine < 12, unwind_panics_observed < 144, leader_changes < 4, minority_proposals < 2, deposed_leader_restarts < 2, messages_dropped < 20, messages_duplicated < 20, messages_reordered < 20, revoke_then_recommit_histories < 14, recoveries_with_acked_revocation < 700, revoked_pairs_denied < 900, crash_points_at_revocation < 140, subjects_min < 3, events_min < 6, probe_calibrated < 1, probe_dirty_seen < 1, probe_clean_checked < 400. Falsified if any of: stale_accepts > 0 (the PtrRuntime replayed over a recovered history authorizes a (subject, generation) that the oracle's reading of that history does not, or that an acknowledged revocation names); acked_revocation_missing > 0 (a recovered history, or a restarted or healed Raft member, lacks a revocation that was acknowledged); recovered_not_prefix > 0 (a recovered history is not the acknowledged prefix plus at most the record in flight, exactly (a record lost, changed, reordered or never sent)); reorder_or_duplicate_index > 0 (the commit indices of a recovered history are not 1 to n, each once); unclassified_split > 0 (the product's classification of a log and its anchor (Aligned, Unacknowledged, LostSuffix) differs from the harness's own table for that pair of files, or an unsafe pair is refused under another name); unjustified_refusals > 0 (the product refused a log and anchor pair that the table says is recoverable (including an image whose bytes after the synced length are all zero), or a recovered ledger could not append the next event and survive a reopen, or a Raft member could not be opened again from its own directory); raft_revocation_visible_before_commit > 0 (a revocation proposed by an isolated leader, which no majority ever held, appears in some member's committed events); product_panics > 0 (a product call panicked (a recovery, a replay, an authorization or a Raft scenario)); product_hangs > 0 (a recovery, an in-process run of appends or a child process outlived its watchdog (60 s)); unsynced_acks > 0 (the durability probe found a page not yet written to disk in a file the product had just called durable, before it wrote the next record, before it renamed the anchor's scratch file or before it moved the anchor; or a RaftEngineLedger append returned without reaching the sync of the engine's log file); authority_mismatches > 0 (the runtime refuses a history the oracle calls valid, or its answer for a pair (may an action proceed, what is the generation's standing) differs from the oracle's without being a stale accept); reference_mismatches > 0 (a baseline run without a fault fails: its recovery trips another falsifier, its append or its creation fails, a child process of the valid workload fails, ends in another way than the abort it was asked for, or does not acknowledge what the run without a fault did, a Raft proposal a leader must accept is refused, or the engine does not reopen on the records it acknowledged); anchored_lie_accepted > 0 (the anchored product recovered (opened) a lie image, a log that lost an acknowledged record or an anchor older than the epoch the host retained, instead of refusing it); refusal_share_excess > 0 (the share of the recoveries of power-loss images that hold zeroed sectors after the synced length which the product refused exceeds the pinned bound (max_refused_share_damaged_permille)); any one of the 5 listed seeds misses any criterion above (every seed must pass). undetected_rollback and engine_lie_stale_accepts (RaftEngineLedger has no anchor), the refusals, the baselines' numbers and every wall-clock time are descriptive and never judged.
